title: lupinus polyphyllus var. pallidipes
intro: Lupinus polyphyllus var. pallidipes, commonly known as the pale-leafed lupine, is a variety of the annual lupine plant that is native to the Pacific Northwest region of North America. It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, which include promoting respiratory health and providing relief from coughs and colds. The plant's therapeutic actions are attributed to its anti-inflammatory and expectorant properties, which help to ease congestion and promote mucus clearance. The bioactive constituents of Lupinus polyphyllus var. pallidipes include alkaloids, glycosides, and saponins, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
